personality.description: This person tends to keep a flexible routine, staying organized enough to meet commitments while still leaving room for spontaneous ideas and creative detours. They actively seek out new perspectives, enjoy experimenting with unusual approaches, and often revisit assumptions to see whether a better explanation exists. In moral dilemmas, they usually stay calm, weigh the practical and ethical sides carefully, and try to find a fair solution without becoming overly defensive, though they will stand their ground if they think a principle is being overlooked. In group discussions, they speak in a balanced, thoughtful way: they listen well, contribute ideas confidently, and shift smoothly between collaborative dialogue and independent reflection.
traits: has assertively moved up the ranks into positions of leadership
prioritizes having control and authority over others
makes quick and definitive decisions, and once a decision is made it is usually final
has their own views of how tasks should be accomplished
uses reward and punishment to get people to follow their ideas
